quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #13
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: When should you yield to a pedestrian?

options.text: Only if they are in a crosswalk.
Always, even if they are breaking traffic laws.
Only if the traffic light favors them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always, even if they are breaking traffic laws.
questions.explanation: Watch for pedestrians near your vehicle at all times. You must do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian, no matter what the situation is.

questions.question: How do you see traffic behind you?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror often.
Turn and look out your back window.
Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your rearview mirror often.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirror regularly to stay aware of vehicles behind you.

questions.question: You are parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the edge of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the edge of the road
questions.explanation: When parking downhill with no curb, turn your wheels toward the road edge. This way, if your brakes fail, your car will roll away from traffic. When parking uphill with no curb, also turn toward the edge. If there is a curb and you are parking downhill, turn toward the center. If there is a curb and you are parking uphill, turn away from the center.

questions.question: What lights should you use when weather or darkness requires lights?

options.text: Parking lights.
High beams.
Low beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, snow, or rain. High beams reflect light back at you, creating glare and making it harder to see.

questions.question: What does a blood alcohol level of 0.02 percent do?

options.text: It has no effect on your driving.
It does not put other drivers at risk.
It doubles your chances of having an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: It doubles your chances of having an accident.
questions.explanation: Every 0.02 percent increase in blood alcohol nearly doubles your risk of being in a serious crash.

questions.question: What should you do to pass safely on a two-lane road?

options.text: Sound your horn as you pass.
Flash your headlights as you pass.
Check how far away oncoming vehicles are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check how far away oncoming vehicles are.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast oncoming vehicles are moving. They may seem slower than they really are. Only pass when you are sure you have enough space to change lanes safely. If you are not sure about an oncoming vehicle's speed, wait until it passes before you pass.

questions.question: What must you do when a school bus is loading or unloading children?

options.text: Stop, no matter which direction you are traveling.
Stop only if you are traveling in the same direction.
Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, no matter which direction you are traveling.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop before reaching a school bus that is loading or unloading passengers, regardless of which direction you are traveling.

questions.question: How should you yield to an emergency vehicle using its siren and lights?

options.text: Drive to the right edge of the road as far as possible and stop.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
Stop immediately, even if you are in an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right edge of the road as far as possible and stop.
questions.explanation: You must yield to any emergency vehicle using its siren and lights. Drive to the right edge of the road and stop. Do not stop in an intersection. You can move again after the vehicle passes.

questions.question: When can you pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a hill or curve.
On a road with a solid line next to your lane.
On a road with a broken line next to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a road with a broken line next to your lane.
questions.explanation: A broken line means drivers can cross from either lane. A dashed yellow line with a solid yellow line means you can pass only from the lane next to the broken line, not the solid line. Only change lanes when it is safe.

questions.question: What is the only thing that removes alcohol from your body?

options.text: Drinking caffeine
Eating fatty foods
Time

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time can remove alcohol and its effects from your body.

questions.question: Which statement about drugs and driving is true?

options.text: Any prescription drug is safe if you do not feel drowsy.
Even over-the-counter drugs can affect your driving.
Only illegal drugs can affect your driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even over-the-counter drugs can affect your driving.
questions.explanation: Legal prescription and over-the-counter drugs can harm your driving ability. This includes drugs for colds, allergies, and anxiety. It is illegal to drive while under the influence of any drug that impairs your ability to drive, whether it is illegal, prescription, or over-the-counter.

questions.question: If the rear of your car skids to the left, what should you do?

options.text: Steer to the right.
Steer to the left.
Tap your brakes lightly and shift into neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer to the left.
questions.explanation: If your car skids, take your foot off the brake and steer in the direction you want to go. If the rear skids left, steer left. This helps align the front with the rear and straightens out the car.

questions.question: When parking on a hill, what should you do?

options.text: Let one rear wheel touch the curb.
Use your parking brake and leave the car in "park."
Keep your front wheels parallel to the road if there is no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your parking brake and leave the car in "park."
questions.explanation: Always use your parking brake and "park" when parking on a hill. If there is no curb, turn your wheels so the car will roll away from the road center if brakes fail. If there is a curb, turn wheels toward it when going downhill, or away from it when going uphill.

questions.question: What should you do if your car has a mechanical problem?

options.text: Signal and move to the slow lane.
Stop in your lane and turn on hazard lights.
Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road.
questions.explanation: If your car breaks down on a highway, make sure other drivers can see it. Get off the road away from traffic and turn on your emergency flashers.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines mean?

options.text: Neither lane may pass.
Both lanes may pass.
The right lane may pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Neither lane may pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions. Double solid yellow lines mean passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.question: What is this symbol used for?

options.text: Dangerous intersections.
Slow-moving vehicles.
Yield signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicles.
questions.explanation: An orange triangle on the back of a vehicle means it travels at slow speeds. You may see this on construction equipment, farm vehicles, or horse-drawn wagons. It appears as a solid orange triangle during the day and a hollow red triangle at night.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: Speed up so you can make the turn before the light changes.
You do not need to signal your turn from this lane.
Get ready to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get ready to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the green arrow protection is ending. If you are turning in that direction, prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic before turning.

questions.question: When entering the interstate on a short ramp with no acceleration lane, what should you do?

options.text: Immediately enter the right traffic lane and speed up to match traffic.
Use the shoulder to get up to traffic speed.
Speed up only after you find a gap in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up only after you find a gap in traffic.
questions.explanation: When entering the interstate on a short ramp with no acceleration lane, speed up only after you see a gap in traffic. Generally, you should wait while stopped for a gap to appear.

questions.question: What should you do when driving through a construction zone?

options.text: Stop to watch the workers.
Follow closer to other cars.
Drive through carefully and do not stare at the work.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive through carefully and do not stare at the work.
questions.explanation: Do not stare at unusual things on the road. This slows traffic and causes congestion. Pass through the construction zone carefully and keep your eyes on the road.

questions.question: What should you do if you see animals near the roadway?

options.text: Speed up to scare them away.
Slow down and proceed carefully.
Quickly swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed carefully.
questions.explanation: Slow down if you see animals near the road. They may jump out or change direction suddenly. Animals often travel in groups, so more may be out of sight.

questions.question: It is very foggy. You should slow down and:

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers.
Turn your headlights to high beam.
Turn your headlights to low beam.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your headlights to low beam.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beam light bounces off water and creates glare, making it harder to see. Some cars have fog lights that work with low beams.

questions.question: When driving on the highway, looking far ahead helps you:

options.text: Keep up with traffic.
Avoid sudden braking or sharp turns.
Spot police officers ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden braking or sharp turns.
questions.explanation: Look ahead and be ready to stop or change lanes. This helps you drive safely, use less fuel, and keep traffic moving smoothly.

questions.question: Adjust your rearview and side mirrors:

options.text: Before you start driving.
Whenever you need to use them.
Before you get into the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Before moving your vehicle, adjust your seat, mirrors, and safety belt, and secure loose items. Do not adjust mirrors while the vehicle is moving.

questions.question: Which statement is true about work zones?

options.text: Fines for violations in work zones are the same as normal traffic violations.
You must slow down in work zones.
Slow down only if you see workers.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must slow down in work zones.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop for road equipment. Driving carefully through work zones protects drivers, pedestrians, cyclists, and workers.

questions.question: When a school bus ahead stops on your side with red lights flashing, you must:

options.text: Slow to no faster than 10 mph.
Stop until the lights stop flashing.
Change lanes and pass carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights and a stop arm mean the bus is loading or unloading students. Do not proceed until the lights stop flashing and the arm retracts. Never pass a school bus picking up or dropping off students.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle, it is safe to return to your lane when:

options.text: The driver you passed signals you to return to your lane.
You signal for three seconds.
You see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Make sure you are not too close to the vehicle you passed. When you see both headlights in your rearview mirror, you have enough room to return to your lane.

questions.question: When stopped at a red light with a green arrow, you may proceed if you:

options.text: Come to a complete stop first.
Wait until the light changes.
Are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go in that direction if you are in the correct lane. First yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Crossroad ahead.
Merge.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossroad ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a crossroad is ahead.

questions.question: You drive defensively when you:

options.text: Keep one car length between you and the car ahead.
Look only at the car in front of you.
Keep your eyes moving to spot hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your eyes moving to spot hazards.
questions.explanation: Scan the road ahead for possible hazards. Staring only at the road directly in front is dangerous. Watch vehicles around you too.

questions.question: Pavement is most slippery:

options.text: When it has been raining for several hours.
When rain just starts.
When it has been raining for one to two hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: When rain just starts.
questions.explanation: Pavement is most slippery when rain first begins. Dirt and oil mix with the water, creating a greasy coating.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, you and the driver on your left arrive at the same time. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on your left.
You.
Whoever is signaling to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: You.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at the same time at a four-way stop, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: When approaching someone crossing with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Stop until they are far from your path.
Honk your horn as you pass them.
Drive carefully around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until they are far from your path.
questions.explanation: Stop and yield to blind pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog. Wait until they are well away before proceeding.

questions.question: This yellow sign means:

options.text: There is a sharp turn to the right.
The lane must turn right.
A right turn is allowed on green arrow only.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a sharp turn to the right.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs alert you to upcoming conditions like curves and sharp turns.

questions.question: A steady red arrow on a traffic light means:

options.text: You cannot turn in that direction.
You may turn after stopping completely.
You may turn in that direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn in that direction.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means do not go in that direction. Stop and wait for a green signal.

questions.question: When approaching a blind pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane, you should:

options.text: Honk so they move out of the way.
Yield the right-of-way.
Swerve quickly around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: By law, you must stop and yield to a blind person using a guide dog or white cane. Let them cross safely.

questions.question: If you become drowsy while driving, you should:

options.text: Try to fight the drowsiness.
Take a break.
Take caffeine pills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a break.
questions.explanation: Stop at a rest area to nap, stretch, or change drivers. Caffeine pills are not a safe substitute for rest.

questions.question: When driving near a large commercial vehicle, you should:

options.text: Follow closely to reduce wind drag.
Avoid driving beside it for long periods.
Drive on its right side on curves and hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid driving beside it for long periods.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles have large blind spots on each side. Do not stay beside them.

questions.question: Your vehicle's wheels go off the edge of the pavement. What should you do first?

options.text: Turn the wheel slightly left to get back on the road.
Hold the wheel firmly, release the gas, and brake gently.
Brake hard and turn the wheel sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the wheel firmly, release the gas, and brake gently.
questions.explanation: Hold the wheel steady, let off the gas, and brake gently. Slow down before checking traffic and safely returning to the road. Jerking the wheel sharply can cause you to lose control.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No U-turn.
No turning.
No left turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn to go in the opposite direction at this location.

questions.question: Drivers turning left must yield to:

options.text: Overtaking cars.
Oncoming cars.
No one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Oncoming cars.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to vehicles coming toward you. Only turn when it is safe.
